found: SEVENTEEN parishes in arrondissement Gent hold Bundervoets in the old parish registers, against the one — Evergem — this tree descends from: Balegem, Desteldonk, Drongen, Evergem, Gentbrugge, Hansbeke, Lovendegem, Mariakerke, Merelbeke, Merendree, Oostakker, Semmerzake, Sleidinge, Vinderhoute, Wachtebeke, Wondelgem, Zomergem. Vinderhoute, Wondelgem and Zomergem carry all three registers. This is the first map of the Bundervoet forest and so speaks directly to objective 3. CAVEAT: it is a finding aid, giving surname, parish and which registers only — never a person, a date or a parent — so nothing from it is graftable. Evergem's dho flag does confirm its burial register covers Joannes Bundervoet 1760 and Christoffel 1786.

goal: the record of his loss at sea, 1883 Oostende
query: COD table 'Omgekomen Vissers van Heist tot De Panne': Familienaam = 'Ramon' (0), then correctly as Familienaam bevat 'Ramon' (0); sanity-checked with 'begint met V' which returns 4 rows, so the table is populated

The COD holds other tables that bear on him — Vissers omgekomen op zee 1902-1970 begins too late, but Volkstelling 1798 Oostende, the Kiezerslijsten, the Huwelijksbijlagen Oostende microfilms and the rouwbrieven databank are all untried. goal: test whether the Huwelijksbijlagen Oostende microfilms are searchable online
query: COD 'Huwelijksbijlagen Oostende_Microfilms': FAMILIENAAM bevat 'Bundervoet' (0), begint met 'Bost' (0)
why: BLOCKED, not a miss: the table returns nothing for any query tried, while its sibling Databank Rouwbrieven returns rows for the same kind of query, so this one is a catalogue stub rather than an empty index. Its header says 'Bestand raadpleegbaar op onze computers' with bibliotheeknummer O-1013MM — the microfilms are consulted at FV-Oostende, not online. Marriage annexes carry birth extracts and parents' consents, so this remains the richest untapped document type for the Oostende families; it needs a visit or a request, not another search.
scope: the Huwelijksbijlagen Oostende table only

goal: find any venue that reaches the pre-1796 Bundervoets, where every name index fails
query: FamilySearch full-text: q.text=Bundervoet, place Belgium — 159 hits across unindexed manuscript collections
found: THE PRE-1796 ROUTE. Machine transcription of images nobody indexed: Flanders nobility/fief records spanning 1463-1792, Gent notarial deeds 1746-1757, Belgian militia records. Named in the snippets: Catherine Bundervoet, widow of Jean De Smet, Meirelbeke 1587; and a THREE-GENERATION FIEF CHAIN — Lievin fils de Francois (Alost, 1687), Pasquier fils de Lievin and Lievin fils de Pasquier (both 16 Feb 1700). That is stated descent in the exact century where this tree's Petrus (~1560), Livinus (~1600) and Segerius (~1615) rest on member trees alone. NOTHING GRAFTED: a Lievin holding a fief at Alost is not our Livinus of Evergem for sharing a name and a century. The finding is the venue.

goal: test whether full-text reaches the deep Oostkamp families, where 121 people sit unverified
query: FamilySearch full-text: 'Wittenheyns' (1 hit, a 1657 Bruges notarial mention of Lieuen Wittenheyns), then 'Sabbe Oostkamp' (thousands)
found: IT REACHES THEM, through a document type this project has never used: 'Belgium. Court Records 1639-1700, 1761-1795' are STATEN VAN GOED — estate inventories drawn on a death. The snippets show exactly what they carry: 'staet en inventaris ten sterfhuyse van Andries Sabbe', then the heirs enumerated with ages and marriages — Barbara Therese, Marie Anne, Marie Catharina getrouwt met Jans Renier, Bregitta oudt ontrent 24 jaren, and 'de vijf kinderen van beide deze'. A whole household named at a death, which is the single richest source for reconstructing a pre-1796 Flemish family. LESSON: a thin surname result is not thin coverage. Wittenheyns is genuinely rare; the province is well covered. Search surname + commune.

goal: retrieve the staat van goed for his 1652 Oostkamp death
query: FamilySearch full-text: 'sterfhuyse Sabbe Oostcamp' (101,134 hits — the terms are ORed, not phrased); tried narrowing by the Collectie and Jaar filters
why: NOT a statement about whether the document exists — it is a statement about the tool. Full-text is a discovery instrument, not a lookup: multi-word queries are ORed rather than treated as a phrase, so adding the commune widened the search instead of narrowing it, and the collection and year filters are a dynamic widget that will not drive from a script. It has shown that Sabbe estate inventories exist in quantity for the right region and centuries; pulling out the one drawn on 31 Dec 1652 needs hand-filtering in the browser or patient paging. The catalogue shape is worth recording: province x record type, with spans like Brabant Eigendommen 1273-1964.
scope: the Belgian full-text collections as a whole; no year or collection constraint could be applied through scripting

goal: his 1863 Grez-Doiceau death act, to document him and name his widow
query: AGATHA: 'Thumas Quinart' + Grez-Doiceau + 1863 (0); then 'Thumas' + Grez-Doiceau + 1860-1900 (46 results)
why: No Grez-Doiceau death act for him. CORRECTS AN EARLIER INFERENCE OF MINE: pass 5 saw Thumas/Grez-Doiceau results running 1799-1859 and I took that as a coverage boundary. It is not — this search returns 46 results reaching 1911, so AGATHA does hold Grez-Doiceau Thumas material well past 1859. What is absent is specifically the death acts of the 1860s: his of 1863 and his son's of 1864 are both missing while other act types continue. Two further cautions confirmed: a two-word query ('Thumas Quinart') is ANDed and returned nothing, so a relative's surname narrows too hard; and the Plaats filter again failed to constrain, since a Brussels marriage act appeared under a Grez-Doiceau search.
scope: AGATHA's act analyses for Thumas at Grez-Doiceau across 1860-1900
